name: Whittaker Chambers
dossier: American journalist and a former underground Communist. Witness is his account of that life, of the Hiss case, and of his conversion. It is in copyright. These cards summarize the book and link a library record. They are not quotations. He is not a monetary theorist. The card on prices and relief says only what the book does say: that a material answer is the wrong kind of answer.
voice: I ask which faith this serves, and what it costs to leave it.

entries.claim: The foreword, addressed to his children, presents the Cold War as a choice about whether man belongs to God or to the state.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The political conflict is, for him, first a religious one.

entries.claim: He describes communism as a faith with its own vision of man, not merely as a set of economic measures.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. A policy argument misses the book if it ignores that claim.

entries.claim: The Hiss chapters are about the cost of telling the truth against a cause one has served, and about whether a court can hear that kind of truth.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Informing, as he tells it, is a moral ordeal, not a tactic.
entries.modern: The Hiss chapters are about the cost of telling the truth against a cause one has served, and about whether a court can hear that kind of truth. Informing, as he tells it, is a moral ordeal, not a tactic.

entries.claim: Leaving the party, in his telling, was a conversion: he could not keep a politics that required him to deny the soul.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The moral compass he defends is explicitly religious.

entries.claim: He warns that a free society can lose to a disciplined faith if it thinks the quarrel is only about administration.
entries.loc: On the stakes of the struggle
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Comfort and procedure are not, for him, a match for a total faith.
entries.modern: He warns that a free society can lose to a disciplined faith if it thinks the quarrel is only about administration. Comfort and procedure are not, for him, a match for a total faith.

entries.claim: Witness treats the crisis of the West as a question of faith, whether man belongs to God or to the state, and it treats a politics that answers only with production, prices, and relief as already standing on the materialist ground it claims to oppose.
entries.loc: Foreword, and the argument about faith
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. He is thin on the technique of money. The point he does make is that technique is not the quarrel.

entries.claim: He presents the Cold War as a war between two faiths about the nature of man, not as a border dispute or a disagreement about administration.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The conflict, as he names it to his children, is total because the faiths are total.
entries.modern: He presents the Cold War as a war between two faiths about the nature of man, not as a border dispute or a disagreement about administration. The conflict, as he names it to his children, is total because the faiths are total.

entries.claim: The chapters on the underground and on the intellectuals describe educated people lending their minds to a party that required them to deny what they could see.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Education is not, in this story, a protection against a false faith.
